title: Explainer: What is El Niño? | New Scientist
description: Every few years, a disturbance in the Pacific Ocean is amplified by feedback mechanisms in the atmosphere, unleashing heat and extreme weather around the globe
author: Alec Luhn

title: Urban trees in south-east England can't cope with the changing climate | New Scientist
description: In cities such as London, trees are already struggling with hot and dry summers. Botanists warn that we need to start replacing them with drought-adapted species
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Spectacular feathered dinosaur fossil shows bird-like adaptations | New Scientist
description: An exquisitely preserved fossil found in China shows that many anatomical features seen in birds also evolved independently in another group of dinosaurs
author: James Woodford

title: How will El Niño affect the world? | New Scientist
description: From Australia to California, the UK to Peru, turbulent weather is on the way
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Scientists can’t stop using AI, even when forbidden from doing so | New Scientist
description: When scientists were asked to review papers for a conference without using AI tools, many of them ignored the request and used AI anyway
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Our food system is vulnerable to El Niño, warns UK climate minister | New Scientist
description: Extreme weather could damage harvests worldwide, but the answer is more local food production, not stockpiling, Katie White said in an interview with New Scientist
author: Alec Luhn
